Nyquist is essentially a high frequency at which digital audio breaks down, and can no longer mimic a real analog sine wave. It is double the recording sample rate. So if you record at 44.1khz then Nyquist is 88.2khz; at 48khz(my recommended sample rate, and 24 bit) it jumps up to 96khz and is effectively a non-issue. Being that human hearing is generally around 20hz-20khz, the nyquist theoretically shouldn’t be an issue, but frequency excitement creates even and odd order harmonics that can get introduced into the audible spectrum. Recording at 48khz and above diminishes the harmonics to a point that they don’t audibly effect the sound, and a low pass filter at 20khz will double ensure that.
